Игра Cellar создаёт по‑настоящему пугающую атмосферу: тёмные помещения, тревожные звуки и ощущение постоянной опасности держат в напряжении от начала до конца. Cellar, developed and published by Vertical Skull Games, is a small but memorable indie experience that dives deep into the kind of primal childhood fears that linger into adulthood. The game places players in the role of a child named Lily, who must descend into her home’s basement to retrieve her missing teddy bear, Blackbear the Pirate. What seems like a simple errand quickly transforms into a surreal, maze-like nightmare that blends nostalgic gameplay with quiet psychological unease. At its heart, Cellar is a minimalist exploration of darkness—both literal and metaphorical—crafted through simple mechanics and evocative design. It doesn’t rely on dialogue or exposition to build tension; instead, it creates an atmosphere of discomfort through its confined spaces, ambient noises, and sense of isolation that slowly gnaws at the player.

The game’s presentation is rooted in retro pixel art, but beneath its simple appearance lies a keen understanding of tone. The dimly lit basements, filled with crates, corridors, and small lurking threats, manage to evoke genuine unease without resorting to gore or overt horror. The environment feels simultaneously familiar and alien—a place every player has seen in real life but twisted into something subtly wrong. Each of the eight levels introduces slightly new variations on this theme, with new layouts, obstacles, and lurking dangers. The restrained color palette of browns, grays, and flickering light helps maintain a claustrophobic mood throughout. The pixelated monsters and traps may look primitive, but their presence is enough to keep players on edge as they navigate the tight spaces and listen to the echo of each footstep. It’s a reminder that fear doesn’t always come from what’s visible—it often comes from what the imagination fills in.

Cellar’s gameplay mechanics are deliberately simple but effective. Each level functions as a top-down maze, with players guiding Lily through the basement’s labyrinthine structure to find keys, avoid monsters, and unlock the way forward. It draws inspiration from old-school puzzle classics like Bomberman and Sokoban, where spatial awareness and timing are more important than quick reflexes. The challenge lies in maneuvering around obstacles, pushing crates, and avoiding the patrolling creatures that threaten to end your journey. The simplicity of the mechanics is both a strength and a limitation. On one hand, it ensures that the game is accessible and focused, never overwhelming the player with unnecessary complexity. On the other, it can feel repetitive for those accustomed to modern gameplay variety. Yet within its modest design, there is an elegance—the kind of purity that recalls a bygone era of indie experimentation where atmosphere and theme mattered more than length or mechanical depth.

Sound plays a subtle but crucial role in shaping the experience. The sparse soundtrack, punctuated by distant hums, creaks, and the faint echoes of movement, enhances the sense of dread. There’s rarely any music to comfort the player, which amplifies the impact of each environmental sound. The silence becomes oppressive, making every encounter with a monster or discovery of a key feel weighted. Combined with the confined visuals, this auditory minimalism transforms the game into something that feels almost meditative—a quiet descent into fear that doesn’t rely on jump scares but instead builds slow, lingering tension. The absence of voice acting or cutscenes further reinforces the solitary nature of the experience. You are alone in this basement, left to interpret the darkness in your own way.

Despite its brief runtime—typically around an hour—Cellar leaves a distinct impression. Its story may be minimal, but its emotional undercurrent is strong. There’s a nostalgic melancholy in retracing the steps of childhood fears through adult eyes, recognizing the absurdity of being afraid of a basement while still feeling that primal anxiety all the same. The final moments of the game, when Lily retrieves her lost bear, feel less like a victory and more like a moment of quiet release—a small triumph against an irrational but powerful fear. It’s this emotional subtlety that makes the game stand out among other small indie titles. The developer doesn’t try to stretch the concept beyond its limits; instead, Cellar ends when it should, leaving behind an echo of unease and reflection.

Ultimately, Cellar is a modest but haunting indie game that thrives on simplicity and atmosphere. It doesn’t attempt to compete with larger productions, nor does it need to. It’s a personal, intimate experience—a short dive into darkness that recalls the uneasy feeling of being told to fetch something from the basement as a child and feeling watched by the shadows. The combination of its nostalgic design, focused gameplay, and psychological undertones makes it quietly effective. For players who appreciate minimalist storytelling and classic puzzle exploration wrapped in eerie ambience, Cellar offers a brief but memorable descent into fear and memory. It’s not a grand or complex adventure, but it captures something essential about the nature of childhood terror—the way small spaces and dim lights can become vast and endless when filtered through imagination and dread.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

"Cellar" — это игра, которая, к сожалению, не соответствует ожиданиям и оставляет себя с рядом недостатков, которые могут повлиять на удовлетворение от игрового опыта.
1.	Графика и дизайн: Одним из явных недостатков является графическое исполнение. Оно может показаться устаревшим и неотшлифованным, что снижает общее визуальное воздействие игры.
2.	Ограниченный геймплей: "Cellar" страдает от ограниченности геймплея. Отсутствие разнообразия в механиках и действиях может привести к скучному и предсказуемому опыту.
3.	Отсутствие глубины сюжета: Сюжет в игре оказывается недостаточно развитым и неинтересным. Это лишает игроков мотивации и вовлеченности в игровой мир.
4.	Технические проблемы: "Cellar" может сталкиваться с техническими проблемами, такими как баги, падения фреймрейта и другие аномалии, что вносит негативное воздействие на общее восприятие игры.
5.	Отсутствие инноваций: Игра не предлагает ничего нового или инновационного в своем жанре. Это может сделать ее невыдающейся на фоне других подобных игр.
6.	Отсутствие атмосферы: Важным аспектом многих игр является создание атмосферы, которая погружает игрока в игровой мир. В "Cellar" отсутствует этот элемент, что делает игровой опыт менее увлекательным.
7.	Неудачное исполнение идей: В тех случаях, где игра пытается предложить что-то новое или уникальное, исполнение этого может быть неудачным, что разочаровывает игроков.
В итоге "Cellar" оказывается под различными аспектами подпадающей под критику. Она может не удовлетворять стандартам, установленным современными играми, и не предлагать достаточно вдохновляющий опыт для привлечения широкой аудитории.

Cellar is a badly made 2D retro pixel action/puzzle game where you control a small girl who goes looking for her missing toys in the multilevel cellar of her house.  No, houses are not like that.  Gameplay consists of plotting your path on the grid like levels while searching for/collecting toys and avoiding the monster that is chasing you.  It's a very shallow experience that's eclipsed by most video games, but thankfully there's less than 30 minutes gameplay... which is also another reason not to bother paying money for this. 

From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.

There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.

The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  

Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the GameMaker Studio construction kit/toolset.  This is a very poor quality toolset favoured by amateur developers as it's cheap and requires little in the way of development skill, but unfortunately has very limited capabilities.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.  GameMaker Studio is most commonly used to make retro pixel shovelware and cash grabs.

A strong argument can be made that construction kits like GameMaker Studio should never be used to make games for profit, as the "developer", Vertical Skull Games has done here.  These construction kits are intended to teach people some of the basic principles of game development, and to make small demos to pass around with friends.  They're not intended to replace to actual work of real, professional game developers.  So it's inappropriate when amateurs try to use these for profit, without any actual, real game development effort taking place.  This doesn't result in products that have any real meaningful value for gamers.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

You don't have to take my word about how bad the game is, we can measure the interest in a game by how much people bothered to play it.  Cellar has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the game absolutely failed to capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for finding the first toy, trivial to achieve, you can do this in less than 3 minutes, but less than 8 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the game.  That's a tiny, tiny proportion of gamers who even bothered with this.  Ouch.

Reviewing SteamDB to check how popular this game was with players reveals a surprise... there's a very healthy spike in player counts for the game.  But this isn't consistent with the achievement stats, that show less than 8 percent of players bothered playing the game for any reasonable amount of time.  How is it possible for this game to have so many concurrent players who weren't even playing the game?  Trading cards.  Players will use card idling software to collect the cards and sell them, but this won't trigger any achievements in-game.  That tells us people only really bought this game for trading cards, and that's a damning indictment of the woeful quality.  A closer look at the numbers shows the game just has a couple of players every week running up the game and idling it for cards, then deleting it.  We must ask how it benefits gamers for there to be so many games like this, with no merit as a serious game, that only generate sales from people idling and selling the trading cards.

Cellar is relatively cheap at $1 USD, but it's not worth it. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

This game features a number of suspicious, likely fake positive reviews. The reviews all appear at almost exactly the same time, within 24 hours after the game launched on Steam, all have a direct Steam purchase of the game, and all have very similar wording and writing style.  This is highly unusual given the very low quality of the game and poor player counts.  The "Positive" review score on this game should be taken with a large grain of salt.  This might be done to deceive and scam gamers into paying for a bad product.

《Cellar》是一款冒险解谜游戏，以其独特的地下世界设定和引人入胜的故事情节，吸引了众多玩家的关注。在我深入体验这款游戏后，不禁被其精彩的玩法和出色的表现所折服。

首先从游戏的核心玩法来看设计独具匠心。玩家将扮演一名探险者，深入地下世界，探索各种神秘的地下室和洞穴。游戏通过精心设计的谜题和挑战，让玩家在解谜的过程中逐步揭开地下世界的秘密。每个谜题都富有创意和挑战性，需要玩家运用智慧和观察力来解开，让人欲罢不能。

其次游戏的画面和音效表现出色。画面风格独特，色彩搭配和谐，使得地下世界的呈现既神秘又引人入胜。音效方面，背景音乐和声音效果都相当出色，为游戏营造出一种紧张而充满探索氛围的感觉。这种视觉和听觉上的享受使得玩家能够更加沉浸在游戏的世界中，感受探险的刺激和乐趣。

再者游戏的故事情节和角色塑造也相当精彩。故事情节扣人心弦，充满悬疑和惊喜，让玩家在探险的过程中不断产生好奇心和探究欲。角色形象鲜明，个性鲜明，使得玩家能够更好地理解和感受角色的情感和动机。这种深入的故事和角色塑造使得游戏不仅仅是一款解谜游戏，更是一部引人入胜的冒险故事。

此外游戏中的任务和挑战也设计得相当出色。任务内容多样且富有创意，每个挑战都需要玩家发挥不同的技能和策略来完成。这不仅增加了游戏的趣味性和可玩性，也让玩家在完成任务的过程中获得了更多的成就感和满足感。

最后从性价比的角度来看同样表现出色。相较于其他同类冒险解谜游戏，它在玩法、画面、音效、故事情节和任务挑战等方面都表现出色，而价格也相对合理。这使得这款游戏成为了一款性价比极高的作品，值得玩家购买和体验。

综上所述，在核心玩法、画面音效、故事情节和角色塑造以及任务挑战等方面都表现出色，为玩家带来了一场深入地下世界的神秘之旅。如果你喜欢冒险解谜游戏，那么这款游戏绝对不容错过。我强烈推荐玩家们去Steam上购买并体验这款精彩的游戏！

Cellar is a horror game where you explore a dark and creepy basement.

Story:

You play as Lily. After you wake up and find your teddy bear missing, you venture down into the basement looking for it all while avoiding a large monster lurking down there. That's about as much as story as you're going to get in Cellar as it's not a really a story driven game, with the story just being there as a backdrop. 

Graphics:

The pixel-esque art style Cellar uses is pretty decent, albeit not anything special and comes off as a bit boring at times. Mostly the dark and dreary basement, which all 8 levels all look pretty much identical with very minor additions to keep things fresh from level to level. I feel like since they already went for the unrealistic route, they should have included more outlandish stuff to make it a bit interesting from level to level. 

Audio:

Cellar basically has no audio design apart from the music which is all royalty free tracks. It's rather disappointing how all of these tracks are re-used constantly and honestly I grew tired of the music before I even got midway through the game and considering how short the game is, it's not a good sign. 

Gameplay:

The basic gist of Cellar is that it's a horror adventure game, where you navigate a maze which is your basement where you try to venture deeper to find your teddy. The door leading further down is often locked and you have to pick up a key, but as soon as you do, a monster starts chasing you intent on killing you, so you need to have a route planned out as soon as you pick up a key.

The game gets harder as you go on, with the levels getting bigger and adding more stuff for you to worry about like smaller monsters, valves that blow steam and floor tiles that collapse destroying a path for you. It does get complex, but not to the point where you will get stuck trying to figure out a way to advance. 

I found the difficulty just right even though it does border on being pretty easy. I really enjoyed going through the levels and found figuring out a route to be a nice little challenge and sometimes it does get intense when the monster is right on your tail and the exit is just in your view.

Just like the main page states, there's only 8 levels which took me roughly 40 minutes to finish, but there is some other side stuff for you to do like finding other toys hidden in the basement, but these do nothing and are only there for the achievements you can collect.

Verdict:

Cellar is a small and short game, that you can finish in a single sitting and it's fine for what it is.  I had fun with the 40 minutes it took me to finish, however if it went on for longer, I would have gotten sick of it pretty soon. It's rather easy and I wish there was more variety in levels and their designs, but what's here could still provide you with some fun.

Final Rating:
6/10

Pros:
+ Fun gameplay
+ Pixel art is decent

Cons:
- Royalty free music sucks
- Levels look pretty much identical to one another

Всем привет, я страстно люблю коротенькие игры, занимающие не более пары часов, но это личные предпочтения, которые мало кто разделяет. Сегодня поделюсь своим мнением по поводу игры Cellar, одобрительно подмигивающей моим вкусам.

Игра действительно коротка, я даже не могу точно назвать потраченное на прохождение время, ибо оно смешалось с монотонным идлом карточек. Наше приключение займет около часа, а если вы являетесь охотником на достижения, то увеличивайте сей запас времени в два раза.

Безнравственные родители оставили маленькую девочку одну дома, да не просто оставили, а на всю ночь! Эти пустоголовые люди не заперли двери в огромный подвал, кишащий уродливыми монстрами и зыбкими конструкциями. Либо родители заведомо планировали потерять единственного ребенка, либо телевизор истребил в них все сознание.

Непутевая девчонка просыпается посреди ночи и обнаруживает пропажу любимой игрушки. Конечно же в голову прилетают оригинальные идеи по поиску своего товарища в лабиринтах опасного подвала. Впитавшая умственные способности родителей, либо просто бесстрашная девочка обязана пройти ряд лабиринтов, попутно собирая иные игрушки, потерянные ранее. За побочные поиски вам будут выдавать достижения, но даже не надейтесь овладеть всеми трофеями за одно прохождение.

В подвале все слишком похоже, но подобный дизайн уровней играет на руку самой Cellar, ибо вам нужно изучить план каждой местности, найти запертые двери, ключ к ним, побочную игрушку, а затем уже приступать к цепочке последовательного выполнения плана. Если же вы схватите ключ без понимания карты, то заведомо обрекаете себя на провал задания. Ключик на каждом уровне оберегает самый страшный злодей, покрытый сгустками шерсти, а после похищения ключика он начнет преследовать девочку с такой пылкостью, что убежать от него можно исключительно с пониманием карты.

В игре приятная анимация, в меру забавный сюжет, хорошая музыка и интересный дизайн уровней, сводящий с ума своими коварными ловушками и перестановками. И все же игра коротка, а достижения заставят играть безошибочно, да еще и не один раз, посему я оставил бы нейтральную оценку, которой меня лишили.
15 рублей определенно не жалко на подобную забаву, приятной игры.

En Cellar nos pondremos en la piel de una niña pequeña, quien despierta en mitad de la noche y descubre con horror que su inseparable osito de peluche ha desaparecido. Un breve paseo por la casa le llevará al sótano, donde comenzará la acción. Allí, deberemos ir en busca del osito, recogiendo otros juguetes por el camino, buscando llaves, y escapando del ogro que aparecerá cuando tengamos la llave en nuestro poder.
Los gráficos y la banda sonora están bastante bien, sin ser tampoco brillantes. Acompañan correctamente, sin más.
La jugabilidad es buena. Sencillos controles y suavidad de movimientos que en seguida manejaremos con facilidad. La dificultad, bien trabajada, se mantiene siempre a un nivel no demasiado alto.
Sus ocho niveles, cada uno de ellos un sótano mayor que el anterior, hacen que el juego se me antoje demasiado corto. En dos o tres horas, conseguiremos acabarlo con todos los logros, e incluso en nivel difícil (con el handicap de tener tiempo limitado por nivel) sin demasiadas dificultades.
Así, cada uno de los puntos del título tiene un nivel aceptable y, juntos, conforman un todo bastante logrado. Pero la durabilidad, muy corta, hace imposible que me plantee una nota mayor. Recomendado, pero no un imprescindible.

Короткая игра о блужданиях девочки по огромному подвалу-лабиринту в поисках пропавшего игрушечного медведя. Состоит из шести уровней, которые при должном везении можно пройти за 20-25 минут. Геймплей на каждом уровне строится вокруг поисков ключа и открывающейся им двери на выход; найти оба объекта лучше перед тем, как поднимать ключ, ибо сразу после этого за героиней начнет гоняться монстр (он движется немного быстрее девочки, поэтому игроку необходимо заранее знать кратчайший маршрут до двери).

Чтобы растянуть время геймплея, разработчики сделали так, что для получения хорошей концовки игрок должен пробежать финальный уровень с первой попытки, не попавшись подвальным монстрам - для этого он, естественно, должен хорошо разбираться в архитектуре крупного лабиринта, которая при этом сильно меняется под влиянием "сюжетного" землетрясения (активируется после подбора ключа, одновременно с началом погони от монстра). Сделать это на первом прохождении практически невозможно, поэтому охотникам за ачивками придется дойти до последнего уровня как минимум второй раз, ради шанса сделать все правильно в самом конце. Для тех, кто как следует изучил все лабиринты, предназначен режим "New Game +", предлагающий пройти игру от начала до конца без возможности перезагрузки уровня в случае проигрыша (т.е. "с одной жизнью").

Возможно, Cellar способна понравиться любителям игр-лабиринтов несмотря на монотонность и скоротечность, но ее геймплей не отличается глубиной, да и как "экспириенс" забывается она достаточно быстро (не спасает даже приятная пиксель-артовая графика, которая быстро приедается из-за постоянного реюза ассетов на каждом уровне). Совершенно необязательный проходняк, на который вроде и не жаль потратить полчаса при покупке в сезон скидок, вот только из-за отсутствия интересных геймплейных решений делать это абсолютно необязательно.
